title: End-to-end load bench journal: triage heuristics & micro-observability
body:
Purpose:
Quick, portable lab notes for reproducing and triaging throughput/latency regressions observed in staging and canary runs. Focus is on end-to-end loadbench (client -> edge -> routing -> infer nodes) so we capture interactions that unit tests and isolated microbenchmarks miss.

Summary / motivation:
- Multiple recent alerts where p95 token latency and tail CPU steal rose together during bursts in canary. Dashboard fingerprints show small change in request distribution (more long-context requests) coincident with a code rollout, but root cause unknown.
- This notebook documents a reproducible minimatch, the investigation steps we ran, commands and PromQL snippets, and prioritized follow-ups. Designed to be copy-paste runnable for whoever is on-call.

Quick checklist (first 10m):
- Identify alert signal + time window (alert ID, graph link).
- Snapshot canary vs stable request size distribution (tokens, prompt length).
- Capture top-10 routes by RPS in window.
- Grab flamegraphs from the affected nodes for the window.
- Check GPU utilization, memclock, and cuda-smi stalls.
- If p95 token latency increased but median is fine, look for microburst batching behavior.

Repro recipe (minimal):
1) Recreate canary traffic profile using loadbench harness:
   - command: ./tools/loadbench --profile canary-2025-01-20.json --clients 40 --duration 15m --target https://canary.redwood-inference/internal/infer
   - config notes: profile includes 12% > 1024-token requests, 6% streaming, 82% sync token-only requests.
2) Capture metrics while load runs: node exporter, nv-host, infra logs.
   - prometheus snapshot: curl -s -G 'https://prometheus/api/v1/query_range' --data-urlencode 'query=rate(infer_requests_total[5m])' --data-urlencode 'start=...' --data-urlencode 'end=...'
3) Collect traces for sample requests: set header X-Trace-Sample:1 and route to trace-collector.

Key signals to compare (canary vs baseline):
- per-host qps, per-core steal, and p95 token latency by model (PromQL examples below).
- batch size distribution across nodes (histogram of tokens-per-batch).
- KV cache hit ratio over time and evictions per minute.
- GPU SM utilization, average compute-to-memory ratio.

Useful PromQL snippets to paste into console:
- Traffic by route: sum by(route) (rate(infer_requests_total[2m]))
- P95 token latency (estimate): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by(le,route) (rate(infer_token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])))
- Batch size histogram: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by(le) (rate(infer_batch_size_bucket[5m])))
- KV cache hit rate: rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) / (rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m]) + rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m]))

Flamegraph capture flow (if suspect hot path in runtime):
- On affected node: sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 300 (during load window)
- Convert: sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf-flame.svg
- Look for spike in copy/memset, lock acquisition, or Python GIL waits if using py wrappers.

Hypotheses considered (ranked):
1) Change in batching heuristics increased average batching setup time for long-context requests -> higher p95. (high plausibility)
2) KV cache behavior: new model variant caused different tokenization/attention leading to more cache evictions -> more recompute. (medium plausibility)
3) Node-level resource contention (IO or cgroup limits) causing CPU steal and throttling at peak. (medium)
4) Routing change sent a small fraction of heavy requests to a subset of nodes causing local saturation. (low->medium)

Experiment log (date-stamped):
- 2024-10-05 09:12: Ran loadbench with shifted token distribution; observed p95 +18% on canary nodes. Collected perf record.
- 2024-10-05 09:45: Flamegraph shows increased time in batch-assembly codepath (synchronization).
- 2024-10-05 10:10: Enabled enhanced batching logs (DEBUG) on node pool; found long tail waits for BatchBuilder due to starved worker threads.
- 2024-10-05 11:00: Provisional fix: increase worker thread pool from 6 -> 12 for batch assembly; re-run loadbench; p95 back to baseline.
- 2024-10-05 12:20: Canary rollback scheduled for release team; follow-up action to measure cost impact.

Canary comparison technique (statistical guardrails):
- Use paired-window comparison: snapshot 10-minute windows from canary and baseline aligned on clock and similar traffic shape.
- Compare median and p95 with bootstrapped confidence intervals. If p95 delta > 10% and CI excludes 0, escalate.
- Avoid chasing noisy median shifts during low traffic. Focus on relative change in tails and GPU utilization.

Alert triage play (short):
1) Validate alert (is it real? correlated increase in traffic or config change?)
2) Check for release tags: which commit rolled in 30m before alert? (link to CI)
3) If profile points to runtime code, run bisect sandbox: selectively toggle feature-flagged change between canary nodes and re-run microbench.
4) If infra-related, open SRE incident and capture node-level snapshots and oom/kube events.

Bisect sandbox pattern (fast local):
- Use canary pool with indiv nodes toggled: attach one node to stable build, others to candidate build; replay same load profile to see delta. This narrows whether change is systemic or config-local.
- Keep dataset and RNG seed identical to reduce variance.

Artifacts to attach when escalating:
- loadbench profile used (.json)
- Prometheus query results (CSV) for window
- Flamegraph SVGs
- Short recording of nv-smi output and dmesg extracts
- Minimal repro run IDs and timestamps

Open follow-ups / TODOs:
- Add a synthetic microbenchmark that reproduces BatchBuilder lock contention with reproducible seed. (owner: Mei)
- Add adaptive worker-thread autoscaling for batch assembly based on queue length (owner: Liam).
- Add a per-route batch-size SLO and alert if distribution shifts > 2 sigma. (owner: Priya)
- Formalize canary paired-window test into CI so PRs run 5m paired-loadbench on merge.

Notes to on-call engineers (quick tips):
- If you see p95 rise + simultaneous GPU util drop, suspicious of batching stalls (threads blocked waiting for batch).
- If p95 and GPU util both rise, look at model change / longer sequences.
- Use archived loadbench profiles under gs://redwood-loadbench-profiles/ when re-running against historical releases.

Appendix: quick commands and references
- Re-run poisson burst profile: ./tools/loadbench --profile poisson-burst.json --scale 1.25 --duration 10m
- Grab canary nodes list: rcli infra list-nodes --tag canary-2025-01
- Collect disk and network stats: sudo iostat -x 1 300; sudo ifstat 1 300
- Helpful dashboards: "Serving / Tail Latency by Route", "Batching / Tokens-per-batch histogram", "KV cache eviction heatmap" (Console links kept in incident template)

Contact / handoff: Jordan Reyes (primary), Mei Chen (batching owner), Liam O'Connor (infra), Priya Nair (observability).

End of journal entry.
